text:
Alex K: morning -> dawn handoff. quick summary of what hit us in the last 45m so Maya has context.

Alex K: Incident timeline: 03:12 UTC pager for elevated 429s on /v1/generate (model-variant: redwood-7b-q4). 03:18 we started seeing KV-cache evictions spike. 03:28 second pager for tenant-specific errors (tenant: AcmeCorp) reporting 500s when fallback failed.

Maya P: ack. who paged first? any noisy retries from the client?

Alex K: pagerduty-bot: triggered by error-rate alert -> pd-incident-#3421. root cause looks like sudden cache TTL churn combined with a spike of prefix-heavy requests from a small cohort. autoscaler didn't keep up due to policy min=1 and burst window.

Juno (oncall-bot): action log attached: escalated to P1, created incident channel #incident-3421, applied model fallback rule (variant -> redwood-3b-quant).

Alex K: Mitigations applied so far:
- enabled fallback routing to redwood-3b-quant for non-enterprise flows (instant)
- increased dedicated pool autoscale delta by +3 (manual bump)
- temporarily disabled aggressive prefix caching eviction for 20m
- rate-limit sticky clients that were resubmitting rapidly (see CC in incident thread)

Alex K: short commands I ran (if you need to validate):
```bash
prodctl pools scale --pool inference-dedicated-usw --delta 3  # manual bump
prodctl cache tweak --policy prefix-evict --hold 120s
curl -sS https://metrics.redwood.internal/api/alerts/3421/status
```

Maya P: thanks. current customer impact? we notified support?

Alex K: impact: 1.5% global error-rate spike, but for AcmeCorp they saw ~8-10% 500s for 6 minutes before fallback. CS notified (ticket #CS-7892). I DM'd Solutions to offer increased retry/backoff guidance. No SLA breach expected but monitoring closely.

Liam R: are there coverage gaps after your handoff window? any follow-ups that require infra changes?

Alex K: primary is Maya P for next 6 hours. Liam R is secondary and on-call for escalation. Coverage gap note: I'm on PTO from 09:10-14:00 UTC, so if anything long-running that needs deeper kernel-level tracing or kernel-updates, please loop in Eng-Runtime (cc @Liam R) because I won't be available.

Maya P: got it. what's the runbook pointer and checklist?

Alex K: runbooks: https://wiki.redwood/inference/runbooks/kv-thundering and https://wiki.redwood/inference/runbooks/model-fallbacks. checklist I used:
- validate PD incident + severity
- check model routing table (RouteService) for recent changes
- confirm autoscale delta + pool health
- enable fallback for affected routes
- throttle noisy clients by ID
- notify CS + customer-facing comms if >5% error-rate for >5m

Maya P: any open tasks for me right now?

Alex K: next steps for you:
- keep fallback for another 15-30m and watch for regressions
- verify KV cache eviction rate stays low (metric: cache.evictions_per_minute < 50)
- confirm autoscaler returns to normal after load reduces (check pool.active_replicas)
- coordinate with CS for a post-mortem note to AcmeCorp if they request
- if errors persist, escalate to Eng-Runtime and request pprof traces from affected hosts

Maya P: on it. I'll also open a short post-incident note in #postmortems once we stabilize.

Juno (oncall-bot): reminder: tomorrow 08:00 UTC scheduled maintenance for cluster-upgrade in us-west. ensure canary traffic is off before upgrade or shift the maintenance window.

Liam R: pinging Eng-Runtime for trace assist if we need deeper analysis (cc @eng-runtime).

Alex K: one more: keep an eye on latency tail (p99) for model-variant redwood-3b-quant after fallback. sometimes cost-optimizing fallbacks add tail latency due to different batching behavior.

Maya P: noted. I'll monitor p50/p95/p99 and post metrics update here in 10m.

Alex K: thanks — leaving primary to Maya. I'll be reachable via DM for 20m then offline. Good handoff. :thumbsup:

Maya P: thanks Alex. taking over. dropping a quick status update in 10. :coffee:

pagerduty-bot: Incident pd-3421 status -> acknowledged by Maya P.

Juno (oncall-bot): thread pinned to #eng-oncall for visibility.

Maya P: (update 10m) fallback holding, cache.evictions_per_minute down to 12, AcmeCorp error-rate back to baseline. Still watching for ripple effects.

Liam R: standing by for escalation.

Maya P: end of summary. next steps documented; I'll create follow-up tasks if we need a permanent autoscale policy tweak.
